exposure: SARS-CoV-2 infection during the first wave of COVID-19 pandemic
SARS-CoV-2 infection during the second wave of COVID-19 pandemic
cohort: The study included 101 pregnant patients with COVID-19 during the first wave (April 2020 to December 2020) and 22 pregnant patients with COVID-19 during the second wave (March 2021 to July 2021) from a tertiary care hospital in Ayodhya, India.
finding: Second-wave SARS-CoV-2 infection in pregnant women was associated with more lethal adverse maternal and fetal outcomes compared to the first wave.
mod_finding: All cesarean sections in both the first and second waves were performed for obstetric indications only, not due to COVID-19 infection.
